comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the core finding that IL-27p28 deficiency leads to enhanced IFN-γ and T-bet expression in CD4SP thymocytes, RTEs, and naive T cells (C11-C19). OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency across multiple assays; peer reviewers explicitly call this 'unexpected and well described' with 'well-designed and executed' experiments. Both agree on the specificity to Th1 cytokines. Peer review includes C23 (summary conclusion) while OpenEval includes C75 (developmental regulation).

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C28. Both evaluations support that Il27ra-/- mice recapitulate the Cd11c-p28f/f phenotype, confirming IL-27R signaling rather than alternative IL-27p28 functions. OpenEval emphasizes genetic validation; peer reviewers confirm this establishes 'IL-27 as the key cytokine in this process.' No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both evaluations support the epigenetic findings (C4-C5, C29-C36) showing reduced DNA methylation and increased H3K4me3 at Ifng and Tbx21 loci. OpenEval emphasizes specificity controls (unchanged Il4, H3K9me3, H3K27me3); peer reviewers acknowledge the findings but Reviewer 2 considers them 'expected results' rather than surprising discoveries. Both accept data quality and mechanistic link.

Complete agreement on claims C6, C37-C44. Both evaluations support the RNA-seq data showing STAT1-activated gene signature with strong statistical significance. OpenEval highlights qPCR validation and network analysis; peer reviewers find the STAT1 signature 'interesting' and do not question data quality or analysis, though they separately challenge mechanistic interpretation of how STAT1 becomes activated.

Both evaluations support claims C7, C45-C51 showing elevated p-STAT1 Y701 with specificity for STAT1 across developmental stages. OpenEval emphasizes the developmental progression and specificity; peer reviewers acknowledge the data but note it is 'surprising given IL-27 is a potent STAT1 activator.' Both accept the constitutive STAT1 activation finding while questioning its mechanistic basis elsewhere.

Both evaluations support claims C8, C58-C60 showing increased STAT1 binding at Ifng and Tbx21 loci with correlation to H3K4me3. OpenEval notes technical limitation (ChIP after 3 days stimulation) and limited data points for correlations; peer reviewers accept the data ('convincingly affirm the hyper-Th1 phenotype at epigenetic level') but question whether this represents direct causation or downstream consequence.

Both evaluations rate this as UNCERTAIN, though with different emphasis. OpenEval (C52-C57) notes negative controls ruling out SOCS3/IFN-γ feedback are informative but the positive mechanism remains unclear. Peer reviewers (C52-C54, C57, C61, C76-C77, C99) explicitly challenge mechanistic explanation, stating 'A credible mechanistic explanation, cellular or molecular, is lacking' and request additional in vivo models. Both agree the mechanism of STAT1 hyperactivation is unresolved.

Perfect agreement on claims C10, C62-C73, C90-C91, C101. Both evaluations support the autoimmune data showing Cd11c-p28f/f mice alone lack autoimmunity but exacerbate disease in Aire-/- background. OpenEval notes marginally non-significant autoantibody elevation (p=0.068) but significant histological scores; peer reviewers accept the data without disputing statistical interpretation. Both conclude IL-27p28 deficiency alone is insufficient for autoimmunity.

Both evaluations support claims C20-C22 showing equivalent Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg differentiation and CD8+ function under polarizing conditions. OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates specificity to basal CD4+ programming rather than differentiation capacity; peer reviewers accept these as appropriate control experiments. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C84-C85. Both evaluations support the OAS gene upregulation finding from RNA-seq and qPCR validation. OpenEval notes functional significance is unexplored, making it descriptive without mechanistic insight; peer reviewers accept it as part of the broader STAT1 signature without specific challenge. Both treat this as a supported but secondary observation.

Partial overlap on claims C74, C100 (and related C76, C99 in peer R7). OpenEval supports the overall model (C74, C76, C99-C100) while noting speculative elements about STAT1 antagonism. Peer reviewers question whether effects are cell-intrinsic to thymocytes (C3, C74, C75, C100), requesting CD4SP-specific IL-27Ra deletion or bone marrow chimeras. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats; peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN regarding direct versus indirect effects.

Minimal overlap on C23 (summary conclusion). OpenEval R17 groups summary conclusions (C3, C23, C77) as SUPPORTED by combined genetic and functional data. Peer R1 includes C23 with the core phenotype findings (C11-C19) and rates as SUPPORTED. Both agree the integrated conclusion about IL-27p28's critical role is well-supported, though they group related claims differently.

OpenEval R12 evaluates background/rationale claims (C1, C102-C107) as SUPPORTED by prior literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval R13 evaluates literature review claims on IL-27 biology (C2, C78, C108-C126) as SUPPORTED and appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not assess literature review accuracy, focusing on experimental claims.

OpenEval R14 evaluates literature citations on OAS proteins (C79-C83) as SUPPORTED but notes unclear functional relevance to main findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers accept the OAS upregulation data (R11) but do not separately evaluate the cited literature context.

OpenEval R15 evaluates speculative discussion claims (C86-C89, C92-C95) about species differences in autoimmunity as SUPPORTED when appropriately framed as speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not evaluate discussion/speculation claims separately.

OpenEval R16 evaluates clinical relevance claims (C96-C98) citing elevated IL-27p28 in human diseases as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations, though experimental connection is unexplored. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not separately assess translational relevance claims.
